newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-PRECOCIOUS RONALDO TAKES SPAIN BY STORM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PRECOCIOUS RONALDO TAKES SPAIN BY STORM.

text.p: The award of FIFA World Player of the Year to Barcelona's Ronaldo will come as no surprise to the Brazilian striker's fans in Spain.
The brilliant 20-year old has taken the country by storm since arriving from Dutch side PSV Eindhoven last summer for what was then a world record 2.5 billion pesetas ($19.2 million).
Ronaldo has more than justified the fee and has since signed a new contract binding him to Barcelona for the next 10 years.
Ten billion pesetas ($76.8 million) is the price to be paid by any club wanting to buy the young Brazilian, who now earns 500 million pesetas ($3.85 million) a year.
An appropriately astronomical figure for a player the media call the 'extraterrestial' and who seems certain already to be one of the names of the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
Ronaldo, who has exhausted the superlatives of even the most garrulous Spanish commentators, is frequently pictured wearing a spacesuit.
And he has left dozens of opponents wondering what hit them.
Nine of Ronaldo's 15 league goals have come after picking up the ball outside the area and beating defenders.
Compostela supporters gave him a standing ovation after scoring a goal when he picked up the ball in his own half and beat six men.
The Brazilian has earned widespread admiration in a country where strikers diving are more likely to be looking for a penalty than trying to head home a spectacular goal.
Using extraordinary strength and balance, he prefers to bounce off defenders and head for goal rather than hit thr ground and hope to hear the referee's whistle.
Against Valencia, Ronaldo was more reminiscent of an American footballer than a soccer player as he escaped a sandwich by two players and bore down on goal.
His hat-trick in that match earned Barcelona a 3-2 victory and papered over the deficiencies in Bobby Robson's line-up.
It has escaped nobody's attention that Barcelona's loss of form in November coincided with an injury that kept Ronaldo out of several games.
But his performances after reappearing also saw a question mark placed over the man who at the beginning of the season was already being compared with Pele.
Ronaldo is clearly not at his best in the penalty area and missed a simple chance in the crunch match against Real Madrid.

But the New Year -- and perhaps his relationship with a Brazilian model known as 'Ronaldinha' -- inspired Ronaldo to play a great match against Deportivo before ending a 56-day goal-drought against Hercules.
